title: telegram-login.ts prints the new TELEGRAM_SESSION string (full access to the Telegram account) to the terminal and reads the 2FA password with echo on

evidence.note: console.log("TELEGRAM_SESSION=" + sessionString): the secret goes to stdout for the operator to copy into .env
the 2FA password is read through the same echoing prompt

sibling_sites_checked: The NEVER-logged rule stated in pause.ts:13-16 was checked in all 13 scripts: PRIVATE_KEY, DEPLOY_PRIVATE_KEY, DASHBOARD_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_API_HASH and FLASHBOTS_AUTH_KEY values are never logged or passed as argv by any script; DASHBOARD_API_KEY travels only in a request body (pause.ts:91-95, resume.ts:57-61); ETHERSCAN_API_KEY travels in an Etherscan URL query string over HTTPS (audit-honeypot-checker.ts:46, :74) and is not printed. telegram-login.ts is the only script that prints a secret on its success path, by design.
severity_rationale: S3: by design and only when the operator runs the helper, but the printed value is a full account credential for the Telegram account the bot listens with (an attacker with it can read and send as that account, including fake alpha-drop calls the bot trusts, C20). Scrollback, terminal logging or an agent capturing stdout keep it.
recommendation: Phase 29 (HYG-03): write the session into .env directly after a confirmation (atomic replace of the one line) or into a user-only file, and print only a short fingerprint; read the 2FA password and the login code without echo. No trading behaviour changes.
